subject: Efficiency of using local variable in model block vs unmonitored transformed parameter

messages.author: a2d460b4e88b69d8
messages.subject: Efficiency of using local variable in model block vs unmonitored transformed parameter
parts:
Is there any difference between the two options? I'm wondering where I should put together a vector or matrix that has some constrained and some free elements.

Thanks!

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Efficiency of using local variable in model block vs unmonitored transformed parameter
parts:
There is very little efficiency consideration, unless we are talking about a covariance matrix or correlation matrix which are expensive to validate. The main thing is whether you want to store the result, which is probably not the case if it is just a union of constrained and free parameters (which are getting stored already).

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Efficiency of using local variable in model block vs unmonitored transformed parameter
parts:
There's a bit more overhead in the transformed parameters
block because the variable gets stored in an array and then
ignored on output if it's not being monitored. Making it
a local variable in the model avoids any additional copying
and switching.

Plus, as Ben pointed out, you have more options to check
constraints in the transformed parameters block, which can be
expensive for some types like covariance matrices.

- Bob
